item.title: Hiroshima Flower Festival: Golden Week on Peace Boulevard — Guide
item.description: The Hiroshima Flower Festival, held over three days of Golden Week each May, is the city’s largest annual celebration and draws well over a million people. Begun in 1977, it fills the broad Peace Boulevard with flower-decked floats, marching bands, dance teams and stages of music running from the city centre toward the Peace Park, culminating in a huge floral monument. Its founding spirit was explicitly one of peace and recovery, and the effect is striking: the same city that mourns each August turns bright, loud and joyful in spring, and the festival is free and open to everyone.

item.title: Kobe Matsuri: The City's Great Port Parade — Guide
item.description: Kobe Matsuri is the city’s largest annual celebration, filling the centre for a weekend each May. Descended from a 1930s port festival and reshaped after the war, it is deliberately outward-looking, reflecting a port that has always been Japan’s most international city: the main parade down Flower Road mixes samba troupes in full carnival costume with marching bands, floats, dance teams and community groups from Kobe’s foreign communities. Smaller neighbourhood events run across the city’s wards, and the whole thing is free to watch.

item.title: Toyama Matsuri: The City's Summer Festival Celebration — Guide
item.description: Toyama Matsuri is Toyama City’s summer festival, held each year and filling the streets around Toyama Castle Park with parades, traditional dance performances and food stalls that draw residents and visitors together for a lively celebration of local culture. The festival typically includes performances by local dance groups and marching bands, alongside stalls selling festival food and drinks, offering a good introduction to Toyama’s community spirit for visitors passing through the city.
